equations: $100 selling price − $60 variable cost = $40 contribution margin
beats.narration: Imagine a product sells for one hundred dollars and requires sixty dollars of variable cost for each unit. The forty-dollar difference is its unit contribution margin. It is not automatically profit. It is the amount that one additional sale contributes toward fixed costs and, after those are covered, operating profit.
beats.title: Separate variable cost from price
beats.visualDirection: template:showcase-contribution-margin | Show a one-hundred-dollar sale minus sixty dollars of variable cost.

beats.delivery: Professional, concise, and paced for an introductory course audience.
beats.narration: Divide forty dollars by the one-hundred-dollar selling price and the contribution margin ratio is forty percent. That means forty cents of each sales dollar is available for fixed costs and then profit, under the model's assumptions. Ratios make it easier to compare products with different prices.
beats.title: Convert margin into a ratio
beats.visualDirection: template:showcase-contribution-margin | Divide the forty-dollar contribution by the one-hundred-dollar selling price.

beats.delivery: Professional, concise, and paced for an introductory course audience.
beats.narration: Managers use contribution margin to explore break-even volume, product mix, and the effect of changing price or variable cost. The result is only as good as the assumptions. Costs may change outside a relevant range, capacity may be limited, and demand may respond to price. Contribution margin is a decision model, not a substitute for context.
beats.title: Use the result within its assumptions
beats.visualDirection: template:showcase-contribution-margin | Compare product choices and mark the relevant range where price and cost assumptions remain valid.

claims.text: Unit contribution margin equals selling price per unit minus variable cost per unit.
The contribution margin ratio expresses contribution margin as a percentage of sales.
Contribution margin supports cost-volume-profit decisions, but the analysis depends on assumptions about costs, prices, and operating range.

sources.author: OpenStax
sources.excerpt: Contribution margin is sales revenue minus variable costs. Per unit, it equals selling price per unit minus variable cost per unit. The contribution margin first covers fixed costs and then contributes to operating profit. The contribution margin ratio divides contribution margin per unit by selling price per unit and indicates how much of each sales dollar is available for fixed costs and profit. Cost-volume-profit analysis relies on assumptions including a relevant operating range.
